Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 9, verse 73:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾. As for striving against the disbelievers, it is with the sword. Regarding striving against the hypocrites, there are two opinions.

One of them: it is with the tongue. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, and al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas.

The second: striving against them is by enforcing the hudud (prescribed punishments) upon them. This was related from al-Hasan and Qatadah.

(p-470) If it is said: when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was commanded to strive against them, and he knew their individuals, why did he leave them among his companions without killing them?

The answer: he was only commanded to fight those who openly displayed the word of disbelief and persisted in it. As for one who, when his disbelief is discovered, denies it, swears, and says, "I am a Muslim," he was commanded to take him by his outward affair and not to probe into his inner secret.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And be harsh upon them﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: it means severity of rebuke toward them and a look of hatred and loathing. Regarding the pronoun in "ʿalayhim" (upon them), there are two opinions.

One of them: it refers to both groups. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

The second: it refers to the hypocrites. This was said by Muqatil.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 9, verse 74:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They swear by Allah that they did not say [it]﴾. Regarding the occasion of its revelation there are three opinions.

The first: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned the hypocrites and reproached them. Al-Jallas ibn Suwayd said: 'If what he says about our brothers is true, then we are worse than donkeys.' Amir ibn Qays said: 'By Allah, he is truthful, and you are indeed worse than donkeys.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was informed of this, so al-Jallas came and said: 'I did not say anything.' Then the two of them swore at the pulpit, and this verse was revealed." This was related by Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas, and al-Hasan, Mujahid and Ibn Sirin held a similar view.

The second: "'Abdullah ibn Ubayy said: 'By Allah, if we return to Madinah, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it.' A man from the Muslims heard him and informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He sent for him, and he began to swear by Allah that he had not said it, so this verse was revealed." This was said by Qatadah.

The third: "The hypocrites, when they were alone, would revile the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions and attack the religion. Hudhayfah conveyed some of that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they swore that they had said nothing, so this verse was revealed." This was said by al-Dahhak. As for the word of disbelief, it is their reviling of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and their attack upon the religion.

Regarding his saying: ﴿And they planned what they could not attain﴾, there are four opinions.

The first: it was revealed concerning Ibn Ubayy when he said: "If we return to Madinah..." This was related by Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas, and Qatadah said likewise.

The second: it was revealed concerning them when they planned to kill the Messenger of Allah. This was related by Mujahid from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The one meant is a man called al-Aswad." Muqatil said: "They were fifteen men who planned to kill him on the night of al-'Aqabah."

The third: when some of the hypocrites said: "If what Muhammad says is true, then we are worse than donkeys," and a man from the believers said to him: "Indeed, you are worse than donkeys," the hypocrite planned to kill him. That is his saying: ﴿And they planned what they could not attain﴾. This is the view of Mujahid.

The fourth: they said during the expedition of Tabuk: "When we reach Madinah, we will place a crown on the head of 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, to boast of it before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." But they did not attain what they planned.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they found fault only in that Allah and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty﴾. Ibn Qutaybah said: that is, they find no fault in anything, and they acknowledge from Allah only the favour (al-sun'), and similar to this is the saying of the poet:

"The people found no fault in Umayyah except that they are forbearing when angered, ***
and that they are the lords of kings, and the Arabs are set right only by them."

This is not what is meant by finding fault; rather he intended that people find no fault with them in anything. And like the saying of al-Nabighah:

"And there is no blemish in them, except that their swords ***
bear nicks from the clashing of battalions."

That is: there is no blemish in them. Ibn Abbas said: before the arrival of the Prophet (ﷺ) in Madinah they were in hardship in their livelihood, but when he came to them they gained spoils and wealth came to them. On this view, the statement is general. Qatadah said: this refers to 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy. 'Urwah said: it refers to al-Jallas ibn Suwayd, whose client was killed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered his blood-money to be paid, and he became wealthy; then when the verse ﴿So if they repent, it will be better for them﴾ was revealed, al-Jallas said: "I repent to Allah."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if they turn away﴾, that is: they turn away from faith. Ibn Abbas said: as 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy turned away. ﴿Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world﴾ by killing, and in the Hereafter by the Fire.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 9, verse 75:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah﴾. Regarding the occasion of its revelation there are four reports.

The first: that Tha'labah ibn Hatib al-Ansari came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah that He grant me wealth." He said: "Woe to you, Tha'labah! A little that you can render thanks for is better than a lot that you cannot bear." He said: then he asked again, and he said: "Are you not content to be like the Prophet of Allah? By Him in whose hand is my soul, if I wished the mountains to travel with me as gold and silver, they would travel." He said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, if I pray to Allah to grant me wealth, I will surely give every person with a right his right." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, grant Tha'labah wealth." So he acquired sheep, and they multiplied, and Medina became too narrow for him, so he withdrew from it and settled in one of its valleys, until he would pray Dhuhr and Asr in congregation and leave aside what was other than them. Then they multiplied further, until he abandoned the prayers except for Friday, then they multiplied further and he abandoned Friday. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked about him, and he was informed of his condition, and he said: "Woe to Tha'labah! Woe to Tha'labah! Woe to Tha'labah!" Allah, Exalted, revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾ [al-Tawbah: 103], and He revealed the obligatory rules of charity. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent two men to collect the charity, and he wrote them a letter to take the charity, and said: "Pass by Tha'labah and by so-and-so" — a man from Banu Sulaym. So they set out until they came to Tha'labah, asked him for the charity, and read to him the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "This is nothing but a jizyah; this is nothing but the sister of the jizyah. I do not know what this is. Go on until you finish, then return to me." So they went on. He then informed the Sulami, who met them with the best of his wealth. They said: "This is not obligatory upon you." He said: "Take it, for my soul is content with that." So they took from him. When they had finished their charity, they passed by Tha'labah, and he said: "Show me your letter." He said: "This is nothing but the sister of the jizyah. Go on until I consider my opinion." So they went on, and they informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of what had happened, and this verse was revealed up to his saying: ﴿because they used to lie﴾. A man from among the relatives of Tha'labah was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); he went out to Tha'labah and informed him. So Tha'labah came to the Messenger of Allah and asked him to accept his charity. He said: "Indeed Allah has forbidden me from accepting your charity." So he began throwing dust upon his head.

He said: "This is your deed; I commanded you, but you did not obey me." So he returned to his home. The Messenger of Allah passed away and did not accept anything from him. When Abu Bakr became ruler, he asked him to accept it, and he refused.

When Umar became ruler, he asked him to accept it, and he refused.

When Uthman became ruler, he asked him to accept it; he said: "The Messenger of Allah did not accept it, nor did Abu Bakr, nor Umar," so he did not accept it; and Tha'labah died during the caliphate of Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him.

This hadith was narrated by al-Qasim from Abu Umamah al-Bahili.

Ibn Abbas said: Tha'labah passed by a gathering and made them witness against himself: "If Allah grants me of His bounty, I will give every person with a right his right, and I will do such and such."

Then Allah granted him of His bounty, and he broke what he had promised, so Allah related his story to us.

The second: a man from Banu Amr ibn Awf had wealth in Syria, and it was delayed from him, so he suffered greatly. He swore by Allah: "If He brings us of His bounty" — that is, of that wealth — "I will surely give charity from it and surely maintain ties." The wealth came to him, but he did not do it, so this verse was revealed. This was related by Ibn al-Sa'ib from Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas. Ibn al-Sa'ib said: the man was Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah.

The third: that Tha'labah and Mu'attib ibn Qushayr went out before a gathering and said: "By Allah, if Allah grants us provision, we will surely give charity." When He granted them provision, they were stingy with it, so this verse was revealed. This was related by al-Hasan and Mujahid.

The fourth: that Nabtal ibn al-Harith, Jadd ibn Qays, Tha'labah ibn Hatib, and Mu'attib ibn Qushayr said: "If Allah grants us of His bounty, we will surely give charity." When He granted them of His bounty, they were stingy with it, so this verse was revealed. This was related by al-Dahhak.

As for the interpretation: His saying ﴿And among them﴾ means the hypocrites, ﴿are those who made a covenant with Allah﴾, that is, they said: "The covenant of Allah is upon me" ﴿(that we will surely give charity)﴾. The original is "latatasaddaqanna," so the taa' was assimilated into the saad because they are close to each other.

﴿and that we will surely be among the righteous﴾, that is, that we will surely do what the people of righteousness do with their wealth, of maintaining ties of kinship and spending in goodness. Kahmas related from Ma'bad ibn Thabit that he said: "It was only something they intended in themselves and did not speak aloud. Did you not hear His saying: ﴿Do they not know that Allah knows their secret and their private conversation?﴾"?

Allah's saying: ﴿So when He gave them of His bounty﴾, meaning: what they had asked for of wealth, ﴿they became stingy with it﴾ and did not fulfill what they had pledged, ﴿and turned away while they were averse﴾ from their covenant.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 9, verse 77–78:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So He caused them to follow it up with hypocrisy﴾, meaning: He made the outcome of their affair hypocrisy.

Regarding the pronoun in "a'qabahum" (He caused them to follow up), there are two opinions.

The first: it refers to Allah, so the meaning is: Allah recompensed them with hypocrisy. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid.

The second: it refers to stinginess (bukhl), so the meaning is: their stinginess in what they vowed led to hypocrisy as a consequence. This is the view of al-Hasan.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Did they not know﴾, meaning the hypocrites, ﴿that Allah knows their secret﴾, which is what is in their souls, ﴿and their private conference﴾, their talk among themselves.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 9, verse 77–78:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So He caused them to follow it up with hypocrisy﴾, meaning: He made the outcome of their affair hypocrisy.

Regarding the pronoun in "a'qabahum" (He caused them to follow up), there are two opinions.

The first: it refers to Allah, so the meaning is: Allah recompensed them with hypocrisy. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid.

The second: it refers to stinginess (bukhl), so the meaning is: their stinginess in what they vowed led to hypocrisy as a consequence. This is the view of al-Hasan.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Did they not know﴾, meaning the hypocrites, ﴿that Allah knows their secret﴾, which is what is in their souls, ﴿and their private conference﴾, their talk among themselves.

(p-476) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those who criticize the volunteers﴾ — regarding the occasion of its revelation there are two accounts.

The first: when the verse of charity was revealed, a man came and gave a ṣāʿ (a measure), and they said: "Indeed Allah is not in need of this man's ṣāʿ." So this verse was revealed. This was related by Abū Masʿūd.

The second: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf came with forty ūqiyyas of gold, and a man from the Anṣār came with a ṣāʿ of food. Some of the hypocrites said: "By Allah, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān did not bring what he brought except for show, and Allah and His Messenger are surely not in need of this ṣāʿ." This was related by Ibn ʿAbbās.

Concerning this Anṣārī there are two accounts.

The first: that he was Abū Khaythama; this was related by Kaʿb ibn Mālik. The second: that he was Abū ʿAqīl.

Concerning the name of Abū ʿAqīl there are three sayings.

The first: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Bījān; Abū Ṣāliḥ related it from Ibn ʿAbbās. It is also said: Ibn Bayḥān, and it is said: Sayḥān. Muqātil said: he is Abū ʿAqīl ibn Qays.

The second: that his name was al-Ḥabḥāb; this was said by Qatādah.

The third: al-Ḥubāb. Qatādah said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān came with four thousand, and ʿĀṣim (p-477) ibn ʿAdiyy ibn al-ʿAjlān came with a hundred wasqs of dates.

(Yalmizūna) means: they find fault with (yaʿībūna). (Al-muṭṭawwiʿīn) means: al-mutaṭawwiʿīn (those who give voluntarily). Al-Farrāʾ said: the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṭāʾ, so it became a doubled ṭāʾ.

Al-juhd is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz, while the rest of them say al-jahd. Abū ʿUbayda said: al-jahd and al-juhd, with fatḥa and ḍamma, are the same, and their figurative meaning is "their capacity." Ibn Qutayba said: al-juhd is capacity (al-ṭāqa), and al-jahd is hardship (al-mashaqqa).

The exegetes said: by "the volunteers" he means ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and ʿĀṣim, and by "those who find nothing but their effort" he means Abū ʿAqīl. As for His saying, ﴿Allah has mocked them﴾, it means: He requited them for their action, and this meaning has already passed.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 9, verse 80:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask forgiveness for them﴾. The occasion of its revelation: when the threat concerning those who slander (al-lammazin) was revealed, they said, "O Messenger of Allah, ask forgiveness for us," and this verse was revealed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "I will ask forgiveness for them more than seventy times, perhaps Allah will forgive them." Then there was revealed His saying: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 6]. This was related by Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas.

The apparent meaning of His saying, "Ask forgiveness for them," is a command, but it is not so. The meaning is: whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them, they will not be forgiven. It is like His saying: ﴿Spend willingly or unwillingly﴾. The explanation of this meaning has already preceded there. This is the saying of the muhaqqiqun (the verifying scholars). A group went to the view that the apparent wording indicates that if he exceeded seventy, forgiveness for them would be hoped for. Then it was abrogated (nusikhat) by His saying: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them﴾.

If it is said: How was it permissible for him to ask forgiveness for them, when He had informed that they disbelieved?

The answer: He only asked forgiveness for a group of them according to the outward appearance of their Islam, without it being established to him that they had left Islam. It is not permissible to say that he knew their disbelief and then asked forgiveness.

If it is said: What is the meaning of restricting the number to seventy?

The answer: The Arabs use seven for units as a large number, and seventy for tens.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 9, verse 81:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Those who were left behind rejoiced in their sitting (behind) [the Messenger of Allah]﴾. He means the hypocrites who stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the expedition of Tabuk. Al-mukhallaf (those left behind) is the one who is left behind after those who have gone on. "Bi-maq'adihim" means bi-qu'udihim (by their sitting/staying behind). Regarding His saying, ﴿against the Messenger of Allah (khilaf rasul Allah)﴾, there are two views.

The first: its meaning is "after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." This was said by Abu 'Ubayda.

The second: its meaning is "opposing the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." It is in the accusative case (mansub) because it is an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu, object of reason), so the meaning is: they sat (behind) in order to oppose the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This was said by al-Zajjaj. Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Ya'mur, al-A'mash, and Ibn Abi 'Abla read it as "khalfa rasul Allah" (behind the Messenger of Allah), and its meaning is that they lagged behind from jihad.

Regarding His saying, ﴿Do not march out in the heat﴾, there are two views.

The first: it is the saying of some of them to others. This was said by Ibn Ishaq and Muqatil.

The second: they said it to the believers. This was mentioned by al-Mawardi.

They only said this because the weather at that time was extremely hot. ﴿Say: the Fire of Hell is more intense in heat﴾ for whoever opposes the command of Allah.

His saying, ﴿they understand (yafqahun)﴾, its meaning is: they know. Ibn Faris said: fiqh is knowledge of a thing. You say: "faqihtu al-hadith, afqahu-hu" (I understood the hadith); and every knowledge of a thing is fiqh. Then it became specifically applied to the knowledge of the Shari'ah (Divine Law), so whoever knows it is called faqih (jurist).

The author said: Our shaykh 'Ali ibn 'Ubayd Allah said: fiqh, in the general usage of the language, is understanding; and in the usage of the Shari'ah, it is an expression for knowledge of the legal rulings relating to the actions of the responsible persons (mukallafin), such as permissibility, prohibition, obligation, validity, invalidity, liability, guarantee, and other such things. Some prefer to say: fiqh is the understanding of a thing. And some prefer to say: fiqh is the knowledge of a thing.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 9, verse 82:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So let them laugh a little﴾. Its form is that of a command, but its meaning is a warning (tahdid).

There are two views regarding the littleness of their laughter.

The first: laughter in this world is few because of the abundance of its sorrows and worries, and their laughter in it is even less, because of the threat (wa'id) directed at them.

The second: they laugh only in this world, and its duration is brief. ﴿And let them weep much﴾ in the Hereafter. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: "The people of the Fire will weep tears in the Fire, until if ships were sent sailing through their tears, they would sail. Then they will weep blood after the tears. So for the like of what they are in, let the one who weeps weep."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿As a recompense for what they used to earn﴾, that is, from hypocrisy and sins.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 9, verse 83:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So if Allah returns you﴾, meaning: brings you back from the expedition of Tabuk to al-Madinah, (to a group) of the hypocrites who stayed behind without an excuse. He said "to a group" because not everyone who stayed behind from Tabuk was a hypocrite. (They ask your permission to go out) with you to the military campaign.

(p-480) ﴿Say: You will never go out with me, ever, to fight any enemy.﴾ (You were content to sit behind) me (the first time) when you did not go out to Tabuk. Al-Mawardi mentioned two views regarding His saying "the first time":

One of them: the first time you were called. The second: before you asked permission.

As for al-Khalifun (those who stay behind), Abu 'Ubaydah said: al-Khalif is the one who remained behind after the departing traveler, so he sat in his baggage, and he is the one who lags behind the people.

Regarding who is meant by al-Khalifin, there are two views.

One of them: they are the men who stayed behind due to excuses; this was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: they are the women and the children; this was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 9, verse 84:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And do not pray over any of them⦆ (﴿وَلا تُصَلِّ عَلى أحَدٍ مِنهُمْ﴾). The occasion of its revelation (sabab nuzul): when ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy died, his son came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Give me your shirt so that I may shroud him in it, and pray over him, and ask forgiveness for him." So he gave him his shirt. Then he said: "Inform me so that I may pray over him." So he informed him. When he intended to pray over him, ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab seized him and said: "Has Allah not forbidden you to pray over the hypocrites?" He said: "I have been given a choice between two: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 80]." So he prayed over him, and then this verse was revealed. This was narrated by Nafiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar.

Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "My shirt will not avail him against the punishment of Allah the Exalted. By Allah, I truly hope that a thousand of his people will become Muslim because of it."

al-Zajjaj said: It is related that a thousand of the Khazraj embraced Islam when they saw him seeking healing through the garment of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and intending to pray over him.

As for His words "of them" (مِنهُمْ), it refers to the hypocrites. And His words (﴿and do not stand over his grave﴾, وَلا تَقُمْ عَلى قَبْرِهِ). The exegetes said: whenever the deceased was buried, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would stand at his grave and supplicate for him; so he was forbidden from doing that with regard to the hypocrites. Ibn Jarir said: its meaning is: do not take charge of his burial. It derives from your saying: "So-and-so stood (qama) to the affair of so-and-so," and its explanation has already been given earlier.

**Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on Surah al-Tawbah (9), verses 85–89:**

Allah's words, ﴿And do not let their wealth impress you﴾, have already been explained [al-Tawbah: 55].

Allah's words, ﴿And when a surah is sent down﴾: this is general, applying to every surah. Muqatil said that what is meant is Surat Bara'ah (al-Tawbah).

[p. 482] Allah's words, ﴿Believe﴾, meaning: "that you believe." There are three interpretations of this.

The first: persist in faith. The second: do the deeds of one who believes. The third: believe with your hearts as you have believed with your tongues. On this reading, the address is to the hypocrites.

Allah's words, ﴿they ask your permission﴾, meaning: to remain behind. ﴿Those of wealth (ulu al-tawl)﴾, meaning the rich, those who have no excuse for staying behind.

Regarding "al-khawalif" (the ones left behind), there are two opinions.

The first: they are the women. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah, Ibn Zayd, and al-Farra'. Abu 'Ubaydah said: "It is possible that al-khawalif here means the women, and they do not usually form the plural of men on the pattern of fawa'il, although they have said faris (horseman), whose plural is fawaris, and halik (one who perishes), whose plural is hawalik [in a people]."

Ibn al-Anbari said: "Al-khawalif applies only to women, since the Arabs form the plural of fa'ilah as fawa'il, saying daribah (female striker) and dawarib, and shatimah (female reviler) and shawatim. They do not form the plural of fa'il as fawa'il except in two words: fawaris and hawalik. So al-khawalif may mean those who remain behind in the dwellings. It may mean those who oppose and disobey. It may mean the aged women who have no one to defend them."

The second opinion: al-khawalif are the lowliest and most despised of people. It is said: "So-and-so is a khalifah of his family" when he is beneath them. Ibn Qutaybah mentioned this.

As for ﴿was sealed (tuba'a)﴾, Abu 'Ubaydah said its meaning is: "sealed."

﴿Al-khayrat﴾ is the plural of khiyrah. The exegetes have three opinions regarding what is meant by al-khayrat.

The first: they are the most excellent of everything. Abu 'Ubaydah said this. The second: they are the excellent slave-girls. Al-Mubarrad said this. The third: they are the spoils of this world and the benefits of jihad. Al-Mawardi mentioned this.

Allah's words, ﴿they ask your permission﴾, meaning: to remain behind. ﴿Those of wealth (ulu al-tawl)﴾, meaning the rich, those who have no excuse for staying behind.

Regarding "al-khawalif" (the ones left behind), there are two opinions.

The first: they are the women. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah, Ibn Zayd, and al-Farra'. Abu 'Ubaydah said: "It is possible that al-khawalif here means the women, and they do not usually form the plural of men on the pattern of fawa'il, although they have said faris (horseman), whose plural is fawaris, and halik (one who perishes), whose plural is hawalik [in a people]."

Ibn al-Anbari said: "Al-khawalif applies only to women, since the Arabs form the plural of fa'ilah as fawa'il, saying daribah (female striker) and dawarib, and shatimah (female reviler) and shawatim. They do not form the plural of fa'il as fawa'il except in two words: fawaris and hawalik. So al-khawalif may mean those who remain behind in the dwellings. It may mean those who oppose and disobey. It may mean the aged women who have no one to defend them."

The second opinion: al-khawalif are the lowliest and most despised of people. It is said: "So-and-so is a khalifah of his family" when he is beneath them. Ibn Qutaybah mentioned this.

As for ﴿was sealed (tuba'a)﴾, Abu 'Ubaydah said its meaning is: "sealed."

﴿Al-khayrat﴾ is the plural of khiyrah. The exegetes have three opinions regarding what is meant by al-khayrat.

The first: they are the most excellent of everything. Abu 'Ubaydah said this. The second: they are the excellent slave-girls. Al-Mubarrad said this. The third: they are the spoils of this world and the benefits of jihad. Al-Mawardi mentioned this.

**Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on Surah al-Tawbah (9), verses 85–89:**

Allah's words, ﴿And do not let their wealth impress you﴾, have already been explained [al-Tawbah: 55].

Allah's words, ﴿And when a surah is sent down﴾: this is general, applying to every surah. Muqatil said that what is meant is Surat Bara'ah (al-Tawbah).

The Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 9, verse 90:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And those who make excuses came﴾. Ibn Mas'ud recited: "al-mu'tadhirun" (those who offer excuses).

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatada, Ibn Ya'mur and Ya'qub recited "al-mu'adhdhirun" with a sukun on the ayn and a lightened dhal. Ibn al-Samaifa' recited "al-mu'adhirun" with an alif. Abu 'Ubayda said: al-mu'adhdhirun are those who make an excuse without being serious; they merely hint at what they do not do, or show other than what is in their hearts. Ibn Qutayba said: it is said "'adhartu fi al-amr" when one falls short in it, and "a'dhartu" when one exerts oneself fully. Al-Zajjaj said: whoever recites "al-mu'adhdhirun" with a shadda on the dhal, its interpretation is "al-mu'tadhirun", those who offer excuses, whether they have a genuine excuse or not, and here it is more fitting that they have an excuse. They cited the poetry:

Until the year turns, then peace be upon you both, and whoever weeps a full year has indeed offered an excuse.

That is: he has indeed come with an excuse. It is also possible that "al-mu'adhdhirun" refers to those who create the impression that they have an excuse, while they have no excuse. In grammar it is permissible to say "al-mu'idhdhirun" with a kasra on the ayn and "al-mu'adhdhirun" with a damma on the ayn, but they were not recited with these, because pronouncing them is heavy. Whoever recites "al-mu'adhdhirun" with a sukun on the ayn, its interpretation is: those who made excuses and came with an excuse. Ibn al-Anbari said: al-mu'adhdhirun here means al-mu'tadhirun with a sound excuse. The original form of the word according to the grammarians is al-mu'tadhirun; the fatha of the ta' was transferred to the ayn, the dhal replaced the ta', and it was assimilated into the following dhal, so the two became a shadda-ed dhal. In Arabic usage, "i'tadhara" is said both when one comes with a sound excuse and when one comes without one. God Exalted said: ﴿Say: Do not make excuses﴾, which indicates the invalidity of the excuse. Labid said:

And whoever weeps a full year has indeed offered an excuse.

That is: he has indeed come with a sound excuse.

Ibn 'Abbas used to recite "al-mu'adhdhirun" and say: May God curse the excuse-makers. He meant: May God curse the hypocrites among the falterers and others. Al-mu'adhdhirun are those who come with a sound excuse; thus it is clear from this statement that they have an excuse according to the reading of whoever lightened it. Whether they have an excuse according to the reading of whoever doubled it, there are two opinions on this.

The exegetes said: These people came so that they would be granted permission to stay behind from Tabuk, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) granted them permission. Others among the hypocrites sat back without any excuse or showing of a pretext, out of boldness toward God Exalted.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 9, verses 91–93:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak﴾. The scholars differed concerning them: it was revealed in two opinions.

The first: it was revealed concerning ʿĀʾidh ibn ʿAmr and others of those with valid excuses. This is the view of Qatada.

The second: it was revealed concerning Ibn Umm Maktum. This is the view of al-Dahhak.

Concerning who is meant by "the weak," there are three opinions.

The first: they are the chronically disabled and the elderly. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas and Muqatil.

The second: they are the young children.

The third: they are the insane, who were called "weak" because of the weakness of their minds. Al-Mawardi mentioned both opinions. The correct view is that they are those who are weak due to chronic disability, blindness, old age, or physical frailty.

"The sick" are those who have ailments that prevent them from going out to fight. ﴿Nor those who find nothing﴾ are the poor. "Hardship" (ḥaraj) is the constraint of staying behind from the raid, on the condition of sincere counsel to Allah and His Messenger. Concerning this there are two views.

The first: the meaning is when they are free of hypocrisy.

The second: when they guard the families and dwellings.

If the first view is taken, it covers all of those mentioned. If the second is taken, it applies specifically to the poor. He stipulated sincere counsel because whoever stays behind intending to spread corruption is blameworthy. Among sincere counsel to Allah is urging the Muslims to jihad, working to reconcile their relations, and all else that brings about the soundness of the religion.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿There is no way (of blame) against the good-doers﴾, meaning: no path of punishment, because the good-doer, by his goodness, has closed the door of punishment.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Nor upon those who, when they come to you that you might carry them﴾. It was revealed concerning those who wept, and there is disagreement over their number and names. Abu Salih narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "They were six: ʿAbdullah ibn Mughaffal, Sakhr ibn Salman, ʿAbdullah ibn Kaʿb al-Ansari, ʿIlbah ibn Zayd al-Ansari, Salim ibn ʿUmayr, and Thaʿlabah ibn ʿAnmah. They came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ so that he might carry them, and he said: 'I do not find anything to carry you upon.' So they turned away weeping." Muhammad ibn Saʿd, the scribe of al-Waqidi, mentioned in place of Sakhr ibn Salman: Salamah ibn Sakhr, and in place of Thaʿlabah ibn ʿAnmah: ʿAmr ibn ʿAnmah. He said: "It was also said that Maʿqil ibn Yasar was among them." Abu Ishaq narrated from some of his shaykhs that the weepers were seven from the Ansar: Salim ibn ʿUmayr, ʿIlbah ibn Zayd, Abu Layla ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Kaʿb, ʿAmr ibn al-Hammam ibn al-Jamuh, and ʿAbdullah ibn Mughaffal. Some people say: rather, ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr al-Muzani, ʿIrbad ibn Sariyah, and Harami ibn ʿAbdullah, brother of Banu Waqif. Mujahid said: it was revealed concerning Banu Muqarrin, who were seven. Muhammad ibn Saʿd mentioned them, saying: al-Nuʿman ibn ʿAmr ibn Muqarrin. Abu Khaythama said: they are al-Nuʿman ibn Muqarrin, Suwayd ibn Muqarrin, Maʿqil ibn Muqarrin, Sinan ibn Muqarrin, ʿUqayl ibn Muqarrin, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Muqarrin, and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿUqayl ibn Muqarrin. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: it was revealed concerning Abu Musa and his companions.

Concerning what they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to carry them upon, there are three opinions.

The first: it was mounts (dawabb). This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas.

The second: provisions (zad). This is the view of Anas ibn Malik.

The third: sandals (niʿal). This is the view of al-Hasan.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 9, verse 94:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They will make excuses to you﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: It was revealed concerning the hypocrites: "They will make excuses to you when you return from the expedition to Tabuk, so do not accept their excuses, for they have no excuse." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned, they came to him making excuses. Then Allah the Exalted said: (Say: Do not make excuses; we will not believe you.) Allah has informed us that you have no excuse. ﴿And Allah will see your deed, and [so will] His Messenger﴾, if you do good and repent of your staying behind (p-487) ﴿then you will be returned﴾ after death (to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed), and He will inform you of what you used to do in secret and in public.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They will swear to you by Allah﴾. Muqatil said: Some eighty-odd men among them swore, including Jadd ibn Qays and Mu'attib ibn Qushayr.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That you may turn away from them﴾. There are two views concerning it.

The first: that you may overlook their sin.

The second: for the sake of your turning away from them. We have already explained the meaning of rijs (filth, abomination) in surah al-Ma'idah.

﴿They swear to you that you may be pleased with them. But if you are pleased with them, indeed Allah is not pleased with the defiantly disobedient people.﴾

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They swear to you that you may be pleased with them.﴾ Muqatil said: "Abdullah ibn Ubayy swore to the Prophet (ﷺ), 'I will not stay behind from you, and I will surely be with you against your enemy,' and he asked him to be pleased with him. Abdullah ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Sarh swore to Umar ibn al-Khattab, and they kept seeking the pleasure of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said when he arrived in Madinah: 'Do not sit with them, and do not speak to them.'"

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They will swear to you by Allah﴾. Muqatil said: Some eighty-odd men among them swore, including Jadd ibn Qays and Mu'attib ibn Qushayr.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That you may turn away from them﴾. There are two views concerning it.

The first: that you may overlook their sin.

The second: for the sake of your turning away from them. We have already explained the meaning of rijs (filth, abomination) in surah al-Ma'idah.
